results.question: How long are security logs normally kept, and what if they are under an investigation hold?
results.answer:
Security logs are normally retained for 90 days from creation, and SEC-05 likewise says they are retained for 90 days unless attached to an incident or hold. [3][1]

If affected security logs are under a legal, dispute, or investigation hold, deletion is suspended until authorized release, and the scope, custodian, and release decision must be recorded. [4]

SEC-05 states that INC-09 governs incident evidence and DAT-06 governs disposal, but the retrieved passages do not provide INC-09's incident-evidence rules. [1]

sources.title: Information Security and Access Management
sources.text:
Records and metrics
Retain access requests and reviews for one year after closure; retain security logs for 90 days unless attached to an incident or hold. Track overdue vulnerabilities, removal timeliness, device compliance, and repeat exceptions monthly. INC-09 governs incident evidence and DAT-06 governs disposal.

sources.title: Code of Conduct and Speak-Up Procedure
sources.text:
Investigation
An uninvolved investigator sets a proportionate scope, interviews relevant people separately, preserves original evidence, and allows the subject a fair opportunity to respond. Interim measures may include reporting-line changes or access restrictions; they are not findings of wrongdoing. People Operations targets completion within 20 business days and provides a progress update at least every ten business days if more time is needed.

sources.title: Privacy, Information Handling, and Records
sources.text:
Default internal schedule
Policy versions, approvals, and exceptions: three years after supersession or closure. Conduct cases and safety reports: three years after closure. Employment records: three years after departure. Financial transactions, expenses, and supplier contracts: seven years after transaction or contract end, whichever applies. Customer account records: two years after account closure. Support tickets: two years after closure. Incident records: three years after closure. Continuity plans and exercise records: three years after supersession or exercise. Access requests and reviews: one year after closure. Security logs: 90 days from creation. Unsuccessful applicant records: six months after the hiring decision.

sources.title: Privacy, Information Handling, and Records
sources.text:
Overrides and holds
These are illustrative company defaults, not statements of legal minimums. The Privacy Lead records approved jurisdictional or contractual overrides. A legal, dispute, or investigation hold suspends deletion of affected material until authorized release; record scope, custodian, and release decision.

sources.title: Information Security and Access Management
sources.text:
Report and contain
Report a lost device, suspicious login, malware alert, data exposure, or accidental external sharing immediately through the emergency Service Desk channel and notify the IT on-call contact. If that channel is unavailable, call the published internal on-call number. Disconnect a suspected compromised device from networks if safe, but do not wipe it, investigate independently, or delete evidence.

sources.title: Code of Conduct and Speak-Up Procedure
sources.text:
Intake procedure
The recipient forwards the concern to the restricted People Operations queue the same business day. The case owner acknowledges a reachable reporter within two business days, assesses immediate protection needs, and records the allegation, dates, available evidence, and any conflict of interest. Records must not go into a broadly visible Service Desk queue.

results.question: Before disposing of an old laptop, what should happen to sensitive data, and may an unauthorized employee speak publicly for the company about it?
results.answer:
Sensitive information stored on a device such as an old laptop must be securely wiped before disposal or reassignment, and physical records and media should be destroyed according to retention and confidentiality requirements. [1]

No. Only authorized persons may speak on behalf of the company in official external communications, and employees who are not designated spokespeople should avoid public statements that could be interpreted as official company positions and should redirect such questions to the appropriate communications lead. [6][2]

retrievedSources.title: Procurement, Expenses, and Payment Controls
retrievedSources.text:
Reimbursable expenses
Reasonable, necessary business costs are reimbursable when approved and supported. Personal purchases, fines, entertainment unrelated to business, and duplicate claims are not reimbursable. Travel follows WRK-04. Obtain approval against the estimated total before incurring costs; the same FIN-07 thresholds apply to reimbursements.

retrievedSources.title: Procurement, Expenses, and Payment Controls
retrievedSources.text:
Payment verification
Finance matches the approved purchase, receipt confirmation, and invoice, then checks amounts, duplicate invoice numbers, and payment terms. A separate authorized person releases the payment. A worker who changes bank details cannot be the sole verifier or payment releaser.

retrievedSources.title: Procurement, Expenses, and Payment Controls
retrievedSources.text:
Month-end controls
Finance reconciles bank and card activity monthly, investigates unmatched items, and has an independent reviewer sign off. Track overdue claims, missing approvals, duplicate payments, and supplier concentration. Retain approvals, verification evidence, invoices, claims, and reconciliation records under DAT-06's seven-year financial schedule.

retrievedSources.title: Employee Lifecycle and Leave Procedures
retrievedSources.text:
Planned departure
People Operations records the final working date and exact access cutoff time, then opens a restricted departure ticket. The manager assigns handover owners, identifies customer commitments, and confirms company property. IT schedules account suspension for the approved cutoff; email forwarding or data transfer requires an identified business purpose and privacy review. Finance handles outstanding expenses and final payments according to applicable requirements.
